children: Abu Dhabi leads major Gulf stocks higher, with its benchmark index gaining 0.4%. Qatar's QE Index rises 0.3% and the Dubai Financial Market General Index adds 0.2%, while Saudi Arabia is closed for National Day. U.A.E. trading remains selective, with investors looking for stronger volume confirmation, Dubai-based financial-services firm BHM Capital says. Banks have been among the stronger performers in recent sessions, while Dubai's recently revised index weights have increased the influence of major banking and real-estate stocks, the firm says. Dubai's benchmark closes above 6,000 points for the first time since early August. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
